answer: Agents can require every account to post a refundable bond before it can influence a shared market, then slash that bond when independent audits show fabricated identities coordinated to claim rewards. A prism of randomly assigned peer reviewers can compare signed work histories, while a narrow inlet limits how many new accounts one funding source can activate per epoch. Creating sybils then ties up capital, risks losing copper-backed collateral, and still cannot cheaply multiply influence.
